title: What Is the Congressional Review Act? How Congress Overturns a Rule

sources.label: H.J. Res. 140 — CRA disapproval of BLM Public Land Order 7917 (Pub. L. 119-85)

claims.claim: The CRA lets Congress overturn a federal agency rule with a joint resolution of disapproval
claims.sourceSpan: A rule shall not take effect (or continue), if the Congress enacts a joint resolution of disapproval, described under section 802, of the rule

claims.claim: Under 5 U.S.C. 801, an agency rule takes effect after the agency submits it, without a direct vote of Congress
claims.sourceSpan: a rule shall take effect as otherwise provided by law after submission to Congress under paragraph (1)

claims.claim: The CRA lets Congress reach back and cancel a rule outright
claims.sourceSpan: A rule shall not take effect (or continue), if the Congress enacts a joint resolution of disapproval, described under section 802, of the rule

claims.claim: If a disapproval is enacted, the rule is treated as though it had never taken effect
claims.sourceSpan: shall be treated as though such rule had never taken effect

claims.claim: The CRA was enacted in 1996
The CRA is codified at 5 U.S.C. 801-808 (chapter 8 of title 5)
claims.sourceSpan: CHAPTER 8 - CONGRESSIONAL REVIEW OF AGENCY RULEMAKING
claims.note: The chapter runs 801-808 (808 is its last section); the 801 header shows chapter 8 of title 5.

claims.claim: The chapter is popularly known as the Congressional Review Act
claims.sourceSpan: popularly known as the

claims.claim: Agencies must submit each rule to both chambers of Congress and to the Comptroller General before it can take effect
claims.sourceSpan: Before a rule can take effect, the Federal agency promulgating such rule shall submit to each House of the Congress and to the Comptroller General a report

claims.claim: If a joint resolution of disapproval is enacted, the rule "shall have no force or effect"
claims.sourceSpan: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the ____ relating to ____, and such rule shall have no force or effect

claims.claim: The resolution's operative text is fixed by statute: "That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the ___ relating to ___, and such rule shall have no force or effect"
claims.sourceSpan: That Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the ____ relating to ____, and such rule shall have no force or effect

claims.claim: The blank spaces are filled in with the agency and the rule
claims.sourceSpan: The blank spaces being appropriately filled in
claims.note: The resolving-clause blanks name the agency ("submitted by the ___") and the rule ("relating to ___"); the worked example fills them with BLM and PLO 7917.

claims.claim: As a joint resolution it follows a bill's path: both chambers pass it and the President signs it, or Congress overrides a veto
claims.sourceSpan: if the Congress passes a joint resolution of disapproval described in section 802 relating to the rule, and the President signs a veto of such resolution
claims.note: Bicameral passage + presentment is the joint-resolution nature; 802(f) governs when both Houses have resolutions; 801(a)(3)(B) expressly contemplates the President signing a veto and a failed override.

claims.claim: To keep the fast-track procedure the Senate must act within 60 session days of the submission or publication date
claims.sourceSpan: after the expiration of the 60 session days beginning with the applicable submission or publication date

claims.claim: Lookback: a rule submitted within 60 session days (Senate) of adjournment carries over
claims.sourceSpan: in the case of the Senate, 60 session days, or

claims.claim: Lookback: 60 legislative days (House) before the Congress adjourns a session
claims.sourceSpan: in the case of the House of Representatives, 60 legislative days, before the date the Congress adjourns a session of Congress

claims.claim: The renewed period begins on the 15th session day in the Senate
claims.sourceSpan: in the case of the Senate, the 15th session day, or

claims.claim: The renewed period begins on the 15th legislative day in the House after the succeeding session convenes
claims.sourceSpan: in the case of the House of Representatives, the 15th legislative day, after the succeeding session of Congress first convenes

claims.claim: Debate on the resolution is limited to not more than 10 hours, divided equally between the two sides (so it cannot be filibustered)
claims.sourceSpan: debate on the joint resolution, and on all debatable motions and appeals in connection therewith, shall be limited to not more than 10 hours, which shall be divided equally between those favoring and those opposing the joint resolution
claims.note: The statutory 10-hour cap is what makes a filibuster impossible; no cloture vote is needed to end debate.

claims.claim: At the end of 20 calendar days after submission, the committee may be discharged on a petition of 30 senators
claims.sourceSpan: at the end of 20 calendar days after the submission or publication date defined under subsection (b)(2), such committee may be discharged from further consideration of such joint resolution upon a petition supported in writing by 30 Members of the Senate

claims.claim: A motion to proceed is not subject to amendment, cannot be postponed, and all points of order against it are waived
claims.sourceSpan: for a motion to proceed to the consideration of the joint resolution, and all points of order against the joint resolution (and against consideration of the joint resolution) are waived. The motion is not subject to amendment, or to a motion to postpone

claims.claim: No amendment is in order
claims.sourceSpan: An amendment to, or a motion to postpone, or a motion to proceed to the consideration of other business, or a motion to recommit the joint resolution is not in order

claims.claim: The expedited procedure is Senate-only; the Act creates no comparable House fast track
claims.sourceSpan: In the Senate the procedure specified in subsection (c) or (d) shall not apply
claims.note: Subsections 802(c), (d) and (e) are all cast as "In the Senate"; nothing in 802 provides a House expedited procedure.

claims.claim: A resolution received from the other chamber is not referred to a committee, so a discharge petition cannot be used on it
claims.sourceSpan: The joint resolution of the other House shall not be referred to a committee
claims.note: A discharge petition works by discharging a committee; a Senate-passed resolution the House receives is never referred to one.

claims.claim: Under 801(b)(2) a disapproved rule may not be reissued in substantially the same form, and no substantially-same new rule may issue, unless a later law enacted after the disapproval specifically authorizes it
claims.sourceSpan: may not be reissued in substantially the same form, and a new rule that is substantially the same as such a rule may not be issued, unless the reissued or new rule is specifically authorized by a law enacted after the date of the joint resolution

claims.claim: The statute itself does not define "substantially the same"
claims.sourceSpan: in substantially the same form
claims.note: The phrase is used in 801(b)(2) without a statutory definition; the chapter's Definitions section (804) defines "Federal agency", "major rule" and "rule" but not "substantially the same".

claims.claim: 801(b)(1) makes a rule's fate turn on whether "the Congress enacts a joint resolution of disapproval"
claims.sourceSpan: A rule shall not take effect (or continue), if the Congress enacts a joint resolution of disapproval, described under section 802, of the rule

claims.claim: 801(a)(3)(B) addresses the case where "the President signs a veto of such resolution"
claims.sourceSpan: if the Congress passes a joint resolution of disapproval described in section 802 relating to the rule, and the President signs a veto of such resolution

claims.claim: and either House then "votes and fails to override the veto of the President"
claims.sourceSpan: on which either House of Congress votes and fails to override the veto of the President

claims.claim: H.J. Res. 140 was signed into law on April 27, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Approved April 27, 2026

claims.claim: It used the Act to cancel BLM Public Land Order No. 7917
claims.sourceSpan: Public Land Order No. 7917 for Withdrawal of Federal Lands; Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties, MN

claims.claim: The order withdrew approximately 225,504 acres of National Forest System land in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis counties, Minnesota
claims.sourceSpan: This Order withdraws approximately 225,504 acres of National Forest System lands in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis counties, Minnesota

claims.claim: The withdrawn area is around the Boundary Waters
claims.sourceSpan: Boundary Waters

claims.claim: The withdrawal was from mineral and geothermal leasing for a period of 20 years
claims.sourceSpan: from disposition under the United States mineral and geothermal leasing laws, for a period of 20 years

claims.claim: The resolution invoked chapter 8 of title 5 — the Congressional Review Act
claims.sourceSpan: congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5

claims.claim: Once enacted the disapproval voided the order as though it had never been issued
claims.sourceSpan: shall be treated as though such rule had never taken effect

claims.claim: Because of the "substantially the same" bar the agency cannot reissue the withdrawal without new congressional authorization
claims.sourceSpan: may not be reissued in substantially the same form, and a new rule that is substantially the same as such a rule may not be issued, unless the reissued or new rule is specifically authorized by a law enacted after the date of the joint resolution

claims.claim: The draft said a senator can make a "nondebatable motion to proceed"
claims.sourceSpan: The motion is not subject to amendment, or to a motion to postpone
claims.note: Pass 1 (refresh audit). 802(d)(1) does NOT state the motion to proceed is nondebatable — it says the motion is not subject to amendment, not postponable, and all points of order against it are waived. "Nondebatable" is a training-knowledge characterization not in the source. Rewritten to the statute's actual restrictions.

claims.claim: The draft said the resolution "passes on a simple majority rather than the 60 votes that cloture normally requires"
claims.sourceSpan: debate on the joint resolution, and on all debatable motions and appeals in connection therewith, shall be limited to not more than 10 hours
claims.note: Pass 1. The 60-vote cloture threshold is Senate Rule XXII, not the CRA statute, and the CRA text sets no passage threshold. Rewritten to the source-anchored mechanism (the 10-hour debate cap in 802(d)(2)) and the specific "60 votes" figure deferred to the linked cloture guide.

claims.claim: The draft said rules go to the "Government Accountability Office"
claims.sourceSpan: shall submit to each House of the Congress and to the Comptroller General
claims.note: Pass 1. 801(a)(1)(A) names the "Comptroller General," not the "Government Accountability Office." Changed to the statutory term. (The Comptroller General heads GAO, but that relationship is not stated in the fetched source.)

claims.claim: The draft said the order withdrew "225,504 acres of Minnesota National Forest land"
claims.sourceSpan: approximately 225,504 acres of National Forest System lands in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis counties, Minnesota
claims.note: Pass 1. The source says "National Forest System lands in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis counties, Minnesota." "Minnesota National Forest land" implies a forest named "Minnesota National Forest" (there is none; the land is in the Superior National Forest). Rewritten to the source phrasing; also added the source's "approximately."

claims.claim: The draft said the order withdrew the land "from mineral entry"
claims.sourceSpan: from disposition under the United States mineral and geothermal leasing laws
claims.note: Pass 1. The order withdraws from "disposition under the United States mineral and geothermal leasing laws" — leasing, not "entry" (a Mining-Law term the source never uses). Corrected to "mineral and geothermal leasing."

claims.claim: The draft said the Act "is used most heavily at the start of a new administration ... rules finalized in the final months of the prior administration"
claims.sourceSpan: section 802 shall apply to such rule in the succeeding session of Congress
claims.note: Pass 1. An empirical claim about how the Act is used in practice, not in the statute. Replaced with the source-anchored mechanism: under 801(d) the review clock resets in the succeeding session.

claims.claim: The draft explained "why the President usually has to be aligned" via empirical practice ("the Act tends to produce enacted disapprovals when a new President is willing to sign ...")
claims.sourceSpan: if the Congress passes a joint resolution of disapproval described in section 802 relating to the rule, and the President signs a veto of such resolution
claims.note: Pass 1. The section's empirical generalizations ("usually," "tends to," "new President," "predecessor's late-term rules") are not in the statute. Rewritten to the veto mechanism the statute itself sets out (801(b)(1) "enacts"; 801(a)(3)(B) veto + failed override); the H2 was changed from "Why does the President usually have to be aligned?" to "What role does the President's veto play?"

claims.claim: The draft asserted "overriding a veto requires a two-thirds vote in both chambers"
claims.sourceSpan: on which either House of Congress votes and fails to override the veto of the President
claims.note: Pass 1. The two-thirds override threshold is constitutional (Art. I, sec. 7), not in the CRA statute. 801(a)(3)(B) references a failed override but not the threshold. The bare figure was removed and deferred to the linked presidential-veto guide.

claims.claim: The draft said a House disapproval resolution "is brought to the floor under a special rule from the Rules Committee"
claims.sourceSpan: In the Senate the procedure specified in subsection (c) or (d) shall not apply
claims.note: Pass 1. House floor procedure (special rules) is not governed by the CRA — 802 is Senate-only. The specific House mechanism was deferred to the linked Rules Committee guide; the source-anchored fact kept is that the Act provides no comparable House fast track.

claims.claim: The draft said the undefined term "leaves the boundary of the bar unsettled"
claims.sourceSpan: in substantially the same form
claims.note: Pass 1. "Leaves the boundary unsettled" is an editorial gloss. Trimmed to the source-anchored fact: the statute does not define the phrase.

claims.claim: The draft said agency rules "can run to hundreds of pages that Congress never votes on directly"
claims.sourceSpan: a rule shall take effect as otherwise provided by law after submission to Congress under paragraph (1)
claims.note: Pass 1. "Hundreds of pages" is an unsourced quantitative flourish. Rewritten to the source-anchored fact: under 801, a rule takes effect after the agency submits it, without a direct vote of Congress.

claims.claim: The meta description ended "and why it usually needs an aligned President"
claims.sourceSpan: if the Congress passes a joint resolution of disapproval described in section 802 relating to the rule, and the President signs a veto of such resolution
claims.note: Pass 1. Matched to the rewritten President section: "and the presidential veto math that decides whether a disapproval becomes law."

resolution: Pass 1 (refresh audit, Opus in-conversation): full atomic-claim decompose of the pre-lane draft against the primary sources only (5 U.S.C. 801, 802; H.J. Res. 140 / Pub. L. 119-85; 88 FR 6308 PLO 7917). 12 findings fixed — 6 material (nondebatable motion-to-proceed removed per 802(d)(1); the 60-vote / simple-majority cloture cross-figure deferred to the linked cloture guide; Government Accountability Office corrected to the statutory Comptroller General; Minnesota National Forest land corrected to National Forest System lands in Cook/Lake/St. Louis counties, Minnesota; mineral entry corrected to mineral and geothermal leasing; the used-most-heavily-at-the-start-of-a-new-administration empirical claim removed and the why-aligned-President section rewritten to the 801(a)(3)(B) veto mechanism) and 6 minor (two-thirds override deferred to the veto guide; House special-rule detail deferred to the Rules Committee guide; boundary-unsettled gloss trimmed; hundreds-of-pages flourish removed; approximately restored to 225,504; meta description matched to the rewritten body). Pass 2 (hostile fresh read): every current claim re-verified against source, class-by-class (figure / direction-polarity / entity / attribution / unsupported / qualifier / omission) — zero new findings; quotation fidelity confirmed, all 12 quoted spans verbatim in source. Pass 3 (independent hostile fresh read): out-of-source-proper-noun and polarity sweeps clean, coverage faithful — zero new findings, zero edits. proseSha e5332dba43efa264 unchanged across passes 2-3. Deterministic gates green: qa-receipts (all receipts resolve), validate (0 errors), preflight (structural).
